title: Hash Generator
description: Generate SHA-256, SHA-512, SHA-1 and MD5 hashes for text in the browser without sending input to the server.
metaDescription: Generate SHA-256, SHA-512, SHA-1 and MD5 hashes for text in the browser, with security warnings for legacy algorithms.

form.title: Generate text hash
form.description: Paste text, choose an algorithm and format, and copy the digest calculated from the exact UTF-8 bytes.

input.title: Input
input.label: Text
input.privacy: The hash is calculated in the browser. This tool does not send text to the server.
input.exact: Spaces, line breaks, accents, emoji and invisible characters change the bytes and the hash.

options.title: Settings
options.description: SHA-256 is the recommended default. MD5 and SHA-1 are available only for compatibility.

algorithms.label: Algorithm
algorithms.legacyDescription: MD5 and SHA-1 should not be used when collisions or authenticity matter.

uppercase.label: Uppercase hex
uppercase.description: Only affects hexadecimal output; Base64 keeps its own alphabet.

share.title: Share
share.description: By default, the link stores only the algorithm, format and uppercase option.
share.safe: The current link does not include pasted text or generated hashes.
share.publicWarning: Links with content expose the original text to anyone who receives the address.
share.tooLong: The input is too large for a safe link. The link will include only settings and the content flag.

result.title: Result
result.description: The digest uses the exact UTF-8 bytes of the provided text.
result.emptyDescription: Paste text to generate a hash.
result.hashingDescription: Calculating the digest in the browser.
result.tooLargeDescription: The automatic limit is {limit} characters to avoid browser freezes.
result.unsupportedDescription: This algorithm requires crypto.subtle on HTTPS or localhost.
result.errorDescription: The browser could not finish the digest calculation.

recommended.title: Recommended for fingerprints
recommended.description: SHA-2 is suitable for general text fingerprints, but a plain hash does not prove authenticity.

sha1.title: SHA-1 is legacy
sha1.description: Use SHA-1 only for compatibility with older systems, never for new security verification.

md5.title: MD5 is not secure
md5.description: MD5 is useful for legacy checksums, but not for collision resistance, signatures, passwords or authenticity checks.

download.title: Hash Generator
download.caveat: MD5 and SHA-1 are legacy. Do not use plain hashes to store passwords or protect secrets.

comparison.title: Quick comparison
comparison.description: SHA-256, SHA-1 and MD5 are shown together for checking, but the selected algorithm remains the primary result.

hash.title: A hash is a fingerprint
hash.description: The digest changes when any byte changes. It normally cannot rebuild the original text, but simple inputs may be guessed.

encoding.title: Hash is not encoding
encoding.description: Base64 and URL encoding are reversible. A hash is one-way and is used to compare fingerprints.

passwords.title: Not password hashing
passwords.description: Passwords require algorithms with salt and cost, such as Argon2, scrypt, bcrypt or PBKDF2, not plain MD5, SHA-1 or SHA-256.

privacy.question: Is the text sent to the server?
privacy.answer: No. The calculation happens in the browser. Text enters the link only if you explicitly enable the include-input option.

algorithm.question: Which algorithm should I choose?
algorithm.answer: Use SHA-256 as the default for general fingerprints. SHA-384 and SHA-512 are SHA-2 variants with larger digests.

legacy.question: Are MD5 or SHA-1 still secure?
legacy.answer: Not for modern security. They are included for compatibility and legacy checksums, with a visible warning.

encryption.question: Is hashing the same as encryption?
encryption.answer: No. Encryption is meant to be reversible with a key. A hash is a one-way digest for comparison.

passwords.question: Can I use this for passwords?
passwords.answer: No. Password storage needs a dedicated algorithm with salt and cost, not a plain text hash.

exactText.question: Why did my hash change with spaces, breaks or accents?
exactText.answer: Because the tool uses exact UTF-8 bytes. Trailing spaces, CRLF/LF breaks and different Unicode composition change the digest.

sharing.question: Can I share a prefilled text?
sharing.answer: Yes, but only in the link fragment and after enabling include input. Do not use that with secrets.

files.question: Does this tool hash files?
files.answer: No. This version hashes text only. File hashing, HMAC and SHA-3 are outside this scope.

seo.about: The generator calculates text hashes with SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA-1 and MD5 from the exact UTF-8 bytes entered in the browser. It shows metrics, Hex/Base64/Base64URL formats and warnings for legacy algorithms.
seo.howToUseTitle: How to generate an online hash
seo.howToUse: Paste the text, choose the algorithm and output format, then copy the digest or download a summary. Shared links store only settings by default; include the input only when it may become public.
